title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page sits in §2.4 of Grothendieck's May 1966 letter to Tate on crystals, in the case of an abelian scheme f: A→S.

(i) Bicrystal structure. On the cohomology crystal DR^1(A/S), F is the map induced by the relative Frobenius A→A^{(p)}, and V the map induced by Verschiebung A^{(p)}→A. The relations FV = VF = p·id hold on the abelian scheme in characteristic p. Grothendieck transports them to DR^1 using Künneth (postulated in 2.2): it gives H^1(A×A) = H^1(A)⊕H^1(A), so DR^1 is additive in A and multiplication by p induces p. Hence DR^1(A/S) is a 'bicrystal of weight 1', i.e. a Dieudonné crystal.

(ii) Perfect residue field. Over S = Spec k with k perfect, by 1.12 such a crystal is a Dieudonné module over W(k). It should be the classical Dieudonné module of the p-divisible group A[p^∞].

(iii) Construction without the conjectural apparatus of 2.2.
- 1°: S is affine and S→T a nilpotent thickening. A lifts to an abelian scheme B/T, and R^1g_*Ω^•_{B/T} is locally free of rank 2g.
- First affirmation: up to canonical isomorphism this depends only on A/S and S→T, not on the lift B. So A/S defines a locally free crystal DR^1(A/S) of rank 2g. It is additive in A, compatible with base change, and defined for arbitrary S by gluing (marginal addition).
- 2°: Over k perfect, this crystal becomes a free W-module M of rank 2g, with F and V induced by Frobenius and Verschiebung.
- Second affirmation: M is Dieudonné's module. Concretely, for any artinian local Λ with residue field k (a W-algebra canonically, by Cohen's theorem) and any lift B/Λ, there is a canonical, functorial isomorphism H^1_DR(B/Λ) ≅ M⊗_W Λ. Functoriality forces compatibility with F and V.

The next page goes on to the deformation statement: lifts of A correspond to lifts of the Hodge filtration, an equivalence of categories. This is the Grothendieck–Messing theorem in germ.

The aim is a cohomological (crystalline) construction of the Dieudonné module and of the deformation theory of abelian varieties.
errors: The crystal is asserted for arbitrary nilpotent thickenings S→T, with no divided powers. In characteristic p the canonical, lift-independent identification (and the deformation equivalence that follows) is only correct for thickenings with (nilpotent) divided powers, as in Berthelot's crystalline site and Messing's theorem. For the same reason, the 'Second affirmation' for an arbitrary artinian Λ with residue field k needs a PD hypothesis, e.g. it is problematic for k[ε]/(ε^{p+1}). Without divided powers one is on the infinitesimal site, which does not behave correctly in characteristic p.
'Multiplicatif' (replacing the struck-out 'additif') is loose wording. What is used is that Künneth makes DR^1 an additive functor, so that [p] acts as p and FV = VF = p transfers.
Both affirmations are explicitly unverified (stated on the next page). Liftability of abelian schemes over affine nilpotent thickenings is quoted as known; it is true, but non-trivial.

ideas.what: Dieudonné crystal of an abelian scheme defined as the de Rham cohomology of an arbitrary lift to a thickening, independent of the lift

deep.surprise_reason: This is the well-known 1966 letter to Tate, which circulated widely and is the acknowledged origin of crystalline Dieudonné theory and Grothendieck–Messing deformation theory. Everything on the page was later developed and credited to Grothendieck (Messing, Mazur–Messing, Oda, Berthelot–Breen–Messing). The only point of interest is the early, PD-free formulation, which was later corrected.
transcription_corrections: Line 4: 'bi[-c-]cristal' — the typed word is 'bicristal' with a struck letter; read 'bicristal'.

Marginal insertion after 'changement de base': it reads approximately '{+et déf[ini] de façon[?] sans conditions sur S (en recollant)+}'. It is handwritten and partly illegible; 'défini sans condition sur S' is the likely sense.
'Module de Dieudonné {+M+}': the handwritten M is inserted above the comma, i.e. 'un module de Dieudonné M, et:'.
